questions.question: Why is "What does Section 14.3 say about bonus payouts?" risky when no policy text is supplied?
options: Models cannot read numbers in prompts
The question implies an answer exists, pressuring the model to produce something even if there is no such section
The question is too short for the model to process
questions.explanation: Prompts that presuppose an answer, combined with no source text, are a common trigger for fabricated specifics.

questions.question: Which addition most directly reduces the chance of an invented reimbursement figure?
options: "If the policy does not state this, say so and do not estimate a figure. A missing answer is less costly than a wrong one."
"You are a world-class expert on all policies."
questions.explanation: Explicit permission to abstain, with the reason, helps the model choose "I don't know" over a plausible guess.

questions.question: Which citations produced by a model are checkable in the way the lesson recommends?
options: URLs the model recalls from memory
Case names the model believes are relevant
Report titles suggested by the model
Exact quotes tied to a document index from text supplied in the prompt
questions.explanation: Citations pointing to supplied text can be verified directly. Citations generated from memory must be treated as unverified.

questions.question: A model-generated draft for a customer cites a regulator circular number and a calculated total in crore. What should happen before it is sent?
options: Nothing, if the model expressed high confidence
A person verifies the circular against the official source and the figures in a spreadsheet or code
Ask the model to rewrite it more formally
Remove the citations but keep the numbers
questions.explanation: Generated numbers, statutes, circulars, and case citations should never be trusted without checking against the original source; arithmetic is best recomputed in a spreadsheet or code.
